releaseNotes: 12 original AI-drafted 0654 Physics P1 graph questions (motion graphs and load-extension) with 5 checksum-addressed SVG graphs drawn from stored data. Keys recomputed from the graph data by build.mjs. Imported questions enter the super admin AI recheck queue and stay out of student evidence until rechecked.

assets.altText: Distance-time graph for a car. The line rises from 0 m at 0 s to 20 m at 4 s, stays at 20 m until 8 s, then rises to 40 m at 10 s.
Speed-time graph for a cyclist. Speed rises in a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 6 m/s at 3 s, stays at 6 m/s until 8 s, then falls to 0 m/s at 10 s.
Speed-time graph for a runner from 0 to 5 s. Speed starts at 0 m/s and rises along a curve that is steep at first and becomes less steep, reaching about 7.6 m/s at 5 s.

questions.questionText: The graph shows how the distance travelled by a car changes with time. Between which times is the car at rest?
questions.explanation: A horizontal section of a distance–time graph means the distance is not changing, so the car is at rest from 4 s to 8 s.
questions.imageAltText: Distance-time graph for a car. The line rises from 0 m at 0 s to 20 m at 4 s, stays at 20 m until 8 s, then rises to 40 m at 10 s.

taxonomies.evidenceStatement: A correct response supports the ability to identify motion states from the shape of a motion graph. It does not identify every reasoning step or establish mastery alone.

assessmentProfile.sourceReference: Original Brains Heist question; aligned to P1.2.5; https://www.cambridgeinternational.org/Images/664572-2025-2027-syllabus.pdf. Not a Cambridge exam item or endorsement.

questions.questionText: Use the graph to find the speed of the car between 0 s and 4 s.
questions.explanation: Speed is the gradient of the distance–time graph: 20 m ÷ 4 s = 5.0 m/s.
questions.imageAltText: Distance-time graph for a car. The line rises from 0 m at 0 s to 20 m at 4 s, stays at 20 m until 8 s, then rises to 40 m at 10 s.

questions.questionText: Use the graph to find the average speed of the car for the whole 10 s.
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 40 m ÷ 10 s = 4.0 m/s. The time at rest still counts.

questions.questionText: Use the graph to find the distance the cyclist travels between 3 s and 8 s.
questions.explanation: Distance is the area under a speed–time graph. From 3 s to 8 s this is a rectangle: 6 m/s × 5 s = 30 m.
questions.imageAltText: Speed-time graph for a cyclist. Speed rises in a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 6 m/s at 3 s, stays at 6 m/s until 8 s, then falls to 0 m/s at 10 s.

questions.questionText: Use the graph to find the total distance the cyclist travels in the 10 s.
questions.explanation: Add the areas: ½ × 3 s × 6 m/s = 9 m, then 5 s × 6 m/s = 30 m, then ½ × 2 s × 6 m/s = 6 m. Total = 45 m.

questions.questionText: Use the graph to find the acceleration of the cyclist between 0 s and 3 s.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the gradient of the speed–time graph: (6 m/s − 0 m/s) ÷ 3 s = 2.0 m/s².

questions.questionText: Use the graph to find the acceleration of the cyclist between 8 s and 10 s.
questions.explanation: Gradient = (0 m/s − 6 m/s) ÷ (10 s − 8 s) = −3.0 m/s². The negative sign shows the cyclist is decelerating.
questions.imageAltText: Speed-time graph for a cyclist. Speed rises in a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 6 m/s at 3 s, stays at 6 m/s until 8 s, then falls to 0 m/s at 10 s.

questions.questionText: The graph shows how the speed of a runner changes during the first 5 s of a race. Which statement describes the motion?
options: The runner speeds up, and the acceleration decreases.
The runner speeds up with constant acceleration.
The runner speeds up, and the acceleration increases.
The runner moves at constant speed.
questions.correctAnswer: The runner speeds up, and the acceleration decreases.
questions.explanation: The speed keeps rising, so the runner is accelerating. The curve becomes less steep, so the acceleration (the gradient) decreases.

questions.questionText: The graph shows the motion of four objects, P, Q, R and S. Which object moves at the greatest constant speed?
questions.explanation: A straight sloping line shows constant speed, and the steeper line is faster. R is the steepest straight line. S is curved, so its speed is changing.

questions.questionText: Use the straight part of the graph to find the spring constant of the spring.
questions.explanation: Spring constant k = F ÷ x. At 6 N the extension is 12 cm = 0.12 m, so k = 6 N ÷ 0.12 m = 50 N/m.

questions.questionText: At which load does the spring reach its limit of proportionality?
questions.explanation: The graph is a straight line through the origin up to 6 N. After 6 N it curves, so extension is no longer proportional to load.
